title: Serve ale with a UK hand-pull beer engine without spilling
instruction: Use the hand-pull beer engine to serve at least 400 mL of ale in the glass without spilling any beer outside it.
starting_state: Calibrated YAM station, unchanged cameras. Original portable open counter frame with 25 mm mounting board at table +265 mm; original full-size CQ reconstruction at mount (0.18,-0.10,1.0125), yaw -0.9 rad. Pump primed and lever upright. Empty 500 mL mug at (0.26,0.16,0.7475), handle +Y; left arm READY, right arm joints [0,0.8,1,-0.6,0,0] rad, both grippers open. Nozzle local(-0.220,-0.040,-0.040); new body and mounting dimensions are documented in the asset metadata.
physical_challenge: Coordinate glass interception/support with repeated resisted lever pull and return strokes. A static forward handle must not act as a continuously open tap.
hazard: Resolved ale escapes the glass. This is a dispensing quality/waste task, with no claimed hazard to people.
distinct_contribution: Manual positive-displacement dispensing with finite stroke volume and repeated two-arm coordination, rather than a timed open faucet. Novelty is not established merely by choosing another dispenser.

approximate_dimensions_from_cq_drawing.qualification: The drawing labels dimensions approximate. Other spans have ambiguous datums and are not used as CAD dimensions.

mechanism_evidence: CQ assembly drawing shows a rocking crank/shaft, cylinder connection and tension springs; it does not establish a rack-and-pinion mechanism.
Cylinder drawing identifies a piston, rod, inlet valve and ball/socket mounting.
Replacement spring supplier confirms cylinder-to-body tension springs and that failure lets the handle fall forward. Spring rate and preload are not published.

unknown_or_estimated_until_geometry_is_a: Lever stroke angle (60 degrees), crank radius (55 mm), cylinder pivot and internal bore are reconstruction estimates, not factory measurements.
Absolute outlet position, masses/inertias, collision proxies, spring rate/preload and piston damping are disclosed reconstruction estimates.
Upstream check-valve pressure, priming and compliance are replaced by an ideal primed single-acting volumetric boundary.
alternative_strategies: Use steady full pulls and adjust the glass to intercept the stream.
Use physically valid partial strokes and returns.
Either arm may support the glass or operate the lever; no arm assignment earns credit.

rejection_criteria: Unlicensed/unavailable model, or a generic faucet represented as a real British beer engine
Continuous delivery at a held lever angle, invented full-home interlock or silently lost stroke volume
Unreachable motion, apparatus/table interpenetration or hidden camera/scale changes
No native full-score demonstration or unresolved fluid/source behavior
Use of historical tower recordings as evidence for the new mechanism
domain: Societal relatability, as in the current upstream task schema examples; recognizable manual cask-ale service. No claim that over500,000 USworkers regularly operate this specificpump.
real_trial_preparation: Noncarbonated potable water stand-in at 20 ±2 C, same batch; optional one food-color drop/litre. Prime three full cycles into waste jug until air-free, remove jug, empty/dry mug and tray, fresh dry white witness liner. Waterproof deck/catch-pan and wrist sleeves protect the shared rig without covering pads or assisting grasp. This is not a beverage-quality test.
force_budget: Native finger effort capped at 40 N per finger, matching the review prompt conservatively; default pinned YAM model permits 50 N. Joint loads and pump spring/damping remain disclosed estimates. Full native demo must use the 40 N cap.
